_meta.method: Every quote below comes from a page fetched with WebFetch on 2026-10-31. Quotes are the exact sentences the fetch returned; re-check them on the live page before publishing. No doses anywhere.
_meta.fetch_failures: These pages could not be fetched (client_error): vcahospitals.com poisoning page, Merck Veterinary Manual owner edition, Blue Cross UK dog poisoning page, PDSA dog poisoning condition page, ASPCA general poison prevention tips, petpoisonhelpline.com/contact-us, animalpoisonline.co.uk/contact-us. Nothing from these pages is used.

advice.en: Stay calm and act straight away. Panicking or guessing costs time.
advice.sl: Ostanite mirni in ukrepajte takoj. Panika in ugibanje vam vzameta čas.

sources.quote: Stay calm and move your dog away from the source of poison.
it is important to try your hardest to remain calm.

advice.en: Move your pet away from the substance and take away anything that is left, but only if you can do this safely.
advice.sl: Žival odmaknite od snovi in odstranite, kar je od nje ostalo, a le, če to lahko storite varno.

sources.quote: Stay calm and move your dog away from the source of poison.
Remove your pet from the area.
(paraphrased by the fetch, not verbatim) take the substance away from your pet; if they still have some in their mouth, a treat or toy may get them to drop it; wipe off any residue on their fur.

advice.en: Check that your pet is breathing and acting normally. If your pet collapses, has a seizure or struggles to breathe, contact a vet immediately.
advice.sl: Preverite, ali žival diha in se vede običajno. Če se zgrudi, ima krče ali težko diha, takoj pokličite veterinarja.

sources.quote: Check to make sure your pet is safe: breathing and acting normally
(paraphrased by the fetch) if your pet shows signs such as collapse, coma, convulsions, or breathing difficulties, "please contact your vet immediately."

advice.en: Call your vet or an animal poison line right away. Tell them what happened, when and where.
advice.sl: Takoj pokličite veterinarja ali linijo za zastrupitve živali. Povejte, kaj se je zgodilo, kdaj in kje.

sources.quote: Contact your vet immediately – inform them when, where and how the poisoning happened.
Phone your vet straight away
Contact your veterinary team for advice immediately

advice.en: Do not wait for signs of illness. Your pet may seem fine at first; signs can appear hours or even days later.
advice.sl: Ne čakajte na znake bolezni. Žival je lahko sprva videti povsem v redu, znaki pa se lahko pokažejo šele čez nekaj ur ali celo dni.

sources.quote: Never wait to see if your pet develops symptoms.
Even if your pet is acting normal, don't wait to contact APCC.

advice.en: Do not make your pet vomit unless a vet tells you to. It can do more harm than good.
advice.sl: Živali ne silite k bruhanju, razen če vam tako naroči veterinar. Lahko naredite več škode kot koristi.

sources.quote: Do NOT induce vomiting without consulting a vet or Pet Poison Helpline®.
Never attempt to make dogs vomit.
you should never attempt to induce vomiting in your cat.
sometimes it can cause more damage than good.

advice.en: Do not give home remedies (for example salt water, milk or oil) and do not follow random tips from the internet. Ask a vet first.
advice.sl: Ne dajajte domačih pripravkov (na primer slane vode, mleka ali olja) in ne sledite naključnim nasvetom s spleta. Najprej vprašajte veterinarja.

sources.quote: Do NOT give any home antidotes.
Don't use salt water as it's extremely dangerous.
making rash decisions, particularly ones based on information from the Internet, can sometimes cause more problems.

advice.review_note: Sources name salt water and 'home antidotes' generally; milk and oil are our examples, not quoted. Drop them if a vet reviewer prefers.

advice.en: Note what your pet ate, roughly how much and when. Have your pet's breed, age and weight ready for the call.
advice.sl: Zapišite si, kaj je žival pojedla, približno koliko in kdaj. Za klic imejte pri roki pasmo, starost in težo živali.

sources.quote: Contact your vet immediately – inform them when, where and how the poisoning happened.
Gather any leftover packaging or pills to help identify what and how much your pet may have ingested.
the specific AI, percentage and volume ingested are imperative

advice.review_note: The breed/age/weight list is paraphrased from aspca.org/node/61910 (fetch said the page lists breed, age, weight and health); no verbatim sentence captured.

advice.en: Keep the packaging, label, plant or leftovers, and take them (or a photo) with you to the vet, if you can do so safely.
advice.sl: Shranite embalažo, etiketo, rastlino ali ostanke in jih (ali njihovo fotografijo) odnesite k veterinarju, če lahko to storite varno.

sources.quote: If possible, take the packaging, plant or substance to the vet, but only if you can do this safely.
If possible, take the packaging, plant, or substance with you to the veterinary clinic.
make sure you have all product packaging information for the poison in front of you

advice.en: In Slovenia: if you find suspicious poisoned bait, photograph it and report it to the police or the Administration for Food Safety, Veterinary Sector and Plant Protection (UVHVVR).
advice.sl: V Sloveniji: če najdete sumljivo zastrupljeno vabo, jo fotografirajte in prijavite policiji ali Upravi za varno hrano, veterinarstvo in varstvo rastlin (UVHVVR).

sources.quote: Lastnike psov pozivamo, da v primeru suma zastrupitve psa ali druge živali takoj poiščejo veterinarsko pomoč
o zadevi obvesti pristojne službe (policijo ali Upravo za varno hrano, veterinarstvo in varstvo rastlin).

advice.review_note: Source tier C (news site quoting an official appeal). Confirm on a gov.si / UVHVVR page before publishing, or drop.

contacts.hours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year

contacts.fee_quote: When you call or chat with one of our staff experts, a $99 USD per incident fee applies.
contacts.extra: Contact page (https://petpoisonhelpline.com/contact/) also lists 877-416-7319 for the Caribbean and US Virgin Islands and (011)-1-952-853-1716 for other Caribbean islands. Neither page names Canada.

contacts.org: Animal PoisonLine (run by the Veterinary Poisons Information Service, VPIS)
contacts.fee: £35 – £45 per phone call (£35 8am–8pm Mon–Fri; £45 at all other times incl. bank holidays)
contacts.hours_quote: We are open 24 hours a day!
contacts.extra: VPIS itself (https://www.vpisglobal.com/) is membership-only for vets and points owners to Animal PoisonLine 01202 509 000.

contacts.org: Univerza v Ljubljani, Veterinarska fakulteta – Klinika za male živali (dežurna služba)
contacts.fee_note: Page says the call is free ('Telefonska številka je brezplačna ...'); treatment costs are not stated.
contacts.hours: Emergency number reachable 24 h. On-site duty service: Mon–Fri 19.30–8.00 (plus urgent-only intake 14.00–15.00 and afternoon duty 15.00–19.30), Saturday 14.00–24.00, Sunday and holidays 00.00–24.00. Daytime weekday intake through the clinic's regular triage (from 8.00).
contacts.quote: Za nujne primere smo 24 ur na dan dosegljivi na telefonski številki: +386 (0)30 716 190.
contacts.address: Cesta v Mestni log 47 (contact address) / 51 (location), 1000 Ljubljana – the page gives both; confirm before publishing.
contacts.extra: Dogs and cats only. Duty-vet page https://www.vf.uni-lj.si/dezurni-veterinar confirms the same mobile number ('Mobilna številka za nujne primere' +386 (0)30 716 190, 'Telefonska številka je brezplačna in dosegljiva iz vseh mobilnih omrežij.'). Reception for non-urgent booking: 01 4779 277, info@kmz.si. The same page lists 040 452 972 for wild birds, small mammals and reptiles (limited hours) — not for dogs/cats.

contacts.fee: Consultations with a Poisons Information Consultant available from $79 AUD
contacts.extra: Private service (ABN 89 634 636 418; page metadata credits 'Animal Poisons Centre'); not a government body. Same page lists New Zealand: 0800 869 738.

contacts.org: Sveučilište u Zagrebu, Veterinarski fakultet – Sveučilišna veterinarska bolnica
contacts.hours: 0-24 emergency intake, walk-in without phoning ahead
contacts.extra: No emergency phone: 'Djelatnici hitnog prijema nisu u mogućnosti odgovarati na telefonske pozive.' Urgent patients use the south entrance from Charlesa Darwina street. General faculty line +385 (0)1 2390 111 is not an emergency line.

not_confirmed.tried: Searched vf.uni-lj.si, UKC Ljubljana / Center za klinično toksikologijo, gov.si-related searches and Slovenian news. No animal poison line found. The 24ur.com article on dog poisonings tells owners to seek a vet and report bait to police/UVHVVR and names no poison line. A European survey (research-portal.uu.nl, 'Poison information centres are under pressure because of animal-related poison enquiries') says veterinary poison centres are uncommon in Europe but does not name Slovenia. Conclusion: no national line found; absence not stated by an official source.

not_confirmed.what: Human poison centre (UKC Ljubljana) taking animal calls
not_confirmed.tried: Search did not surface an official UKC page with a number or any statement on animal enquiries. Not included.

Pet Poison Helpline home and contact pages fetched: neither names Canada. animalpoisons.com.au says it serves Canada but is an Australian private service. ASPCA page not checked for Canada coverage. Not included.
Animal PoisonLine contact page failed to load; home page does not mention Ireland. VPIS lists several international numbers but does not say which country each serves and is vets-only. Not included.

gesundheit.gv.at lists German Giftinformationszentren (e.g. Berlin +49 (0) 30 19240, München +49 (0) 89 19 240) but these are human poison centres and the page does not say whether they handle animals. Not included.
Vergiftungsinformationszentrale (VIZ) +43 1 406 43 43, 24-Stunden-Notruf, on gesundheit.gv.at — page does not say it handles animals. Not included.
Zagreb university hospital page states 0-24 walk-in intake but explicitly no phone for emergency staff. No animal poison line found.

notes: Strongest sources: RSPCA, PDSA, Pet Poison Helpline, ASPCA, International Cat Care — all agree on: act immediately, don't wait for signs, don't induce vomiting unless a vet says so, bring packaging. VCA, Merck, Blue Cross, Dogs Trust, Cats Protection and FDA pages were not fetched or failed; consider adding them later. Slovenia: no animal poison line exists to our knowledge — the page should tell Slovenian users to call their own vet or the 24 h emergency number of the UL Veterinary Faculty Small Animal Clinic (+386 30 716 190, dogs and cats, Ljubljana). Consider also telling users that private veterinary clinics in Slovenia often run their own on-call service (not researched/sourced here). ASPCA and Pet Poison Helpline are US-oriented paid services; mark fees clearly. Two PDSA and Animal PoisonLine items are fetch paraphrases, not verbatim — flagged inline. Re-verify every number on the live page before publishing; numbers change.
